item.title: Version 1.293.0
item.description:
What's New in 1.293.0

Added

  • Add a video file to a Recording — press Add Video or Image… beside Record next section, right-click the timeline and choose Add Video or Image Here…, pick File ▸ Add Video or Image…, or just drop a video onto the timeline, and it becomes a Section of its own. Prodoozie copies it into the Recording and turns a phone's tall video the right way up, and a clip of another shape sits inside the frame without being squashed. Captions come only from a microphone track, so a phone video's sound plays but gets no captions.
  • Add a picture or a GIF the same way — the same buttons, and a drop onto the timeline, take a picture or a GIF too, and each becomes a Section of its own. A picture shows for five seconds, and you can drag its end out to a full minute to talk over it. A GIF that loops plays for at least three seconds, so a short one isn't gone in a blink. Anything see-through in them shows as black, and Prodoozie tells you when that happens.
  • Section titles — tick Section Titles in the editor's Text tab to put each Section's name on the video for its first four seconds. A Section you haven't named gets no title, and the title sits above your captions, so they never move.
  • Style your Section titles — choose a dark, light or colored box, or no box at all, and a font and size. A colored box can match your background. Prodoozie picks white or black words for you, so a title is always easy to read on its box.
  • Make a loop for your web page — the new loop button beside Poster frame turns your Recording into a short, silent video that plays on repeat. Pick the moments, speed them up, zoom in, ring what matters and add a label, and watch it play as it will on the page. Saving gives you the video, a picture to show before it plays, and code to paste into your site, and anything you hid stays hidden.
  • Private text is hidden for you — when you stop, Prodoozie reads the new take on your Mac and hides people's names, email addresses, card numbers, keys, links and other text that looks private. The editor says what it hid, and you can show any kind again with one click. Only what's inside your windows is hidden: the menu bar, the Dock and the desktop are left alone. It can miss things, so look before you share. If a take can't be checked, the editor and Save Video tell you. You can turn it off in Settings → Recording.

Changed

  • iRecord is now Prodoozie — the app has a new name, and that is all that changed. Your Recordings, your licence and the permissions you gave all carry over, so there is nothing to do. The app in your Applications folder may still be called iRecord after this update; it is the same app and keeps updating.
  • Hidden areas are blurred, not black — a black box over a page looked like something broke. Anything new you hide, or that Prodoozie hides for you, is now a soft blur in the colours around it. The blur keeps nothing of what was under it, so it can't be undone. Areas you hid before stay as they were, and you can still choose solid or pixelate.
  • The editor shows one thing at a time — the panel beside the video has a row of tabs, one for each part of your video: Look, Camera, Sections, Video, Zoom, Text and Hidden. Click the camera, a caption or a clip and the panel shows what you can change about it; click an empty spot to change the background. The timeline names its rows, the sound has a row of its own that always moves with its picture, and a row appears only when it has something in it. Section titles are switched on in Text.
  • A roomier editor — the timeline's rows are taller with space between them, and its words and times are bigger and easier to read. Opening a Recording makes a small window bigger so the editor has room, and a new install opens at most of your screen.
  • Cursor Zoom no longer offers Manual regions — picking it never zoomed anything: it turned the zoom off while the switch stayed on. It is gone from the list. A Recording already set to it shows Manual (zooms nothing) until you pick another mode, and saves the same video as before.

Fixed

  • Report an Issue reaches us again — it started an email to an old address that no longer gets mail. It now goes to support@mail.prodoozie.com.
  • A recording that stops suddenly keeps what was recorded — if a microphone went quiet for a few seconds, or System Audio was off, a recording cut short by a crash or a forced quit could come back empty. Now it comes back up to the last few seconds, and "saved through" on the recording indicator shows only what is really safe.
  • A new plan starts at its first Section — planning a new Series left an empty Section 1 in front of your plan, so the header counted one Section too many and Record next section opened on the empty one. Your plan now takes its place.
  • A plan fits on the timeline before you record — until something was recorded, the timeline showed only the start of your first planned Section, and zooming out did nothing. Now the whole plan is on screen, and Zoom and Fit work.
  • A take that couldn't be saved is no longer forgotten — if Prodoozie stopped in the middle of a take before any of it was safely written, the next launch said nothing about it. Now it tells you which Recording and Section the take was in, so you know to record it again.
  • Clicks in Prodoozie's own windows are recorded — when you recorded Prodoozie itself, your clicks in its windows were not saved, so Cursor Zoom set to On click never zoomed in on them. They are saved now, and a click made while Prodoozie was busy is no longer missed.

item.title: Version 1.288.1
item.description:
What's New in 1.288.1

Added

  • The plan chat reads links you type — paste your product's website into a message and iRecord reads the page before the AI answers, showing it above the message box like any file you attach. Addresses on your own Mac or network are read only if you add them with +. A slow or very large page gives up after 30 seconds instead of holding up your message.
  • Plans that fit what you make — the Create a Plan sheet asks once whether you usually make presentations, product demos, lessons, tutorials or a mix, and its suggestions and the AI's advice follow your answer. Home no longer calls every video a lecture unless you teach. You can change your answer in Settings → Recording.

Changed

  • Product demos start with the product — the plan chat now asks what your product is called and for a link to its website, then its main features, who it is for and the problem it solves. It no longer assumes the video is about iRecord, and it no longer adds an empty placeholder Section while it is still asking.
  • One zoom slider — Cursor Zoom had two sliders, Smooth and Speed, that did almost the same thing. There is now one, called Smooth.
  • The Camera panel says Section — the switch beside Whole recording now reads Section instead of Each section.

Fixed

  • Closing the plan sheet stops the AI — if you close Create a Plan, or switch AI off, while the AI is still answering, iRecord stops waiting for it. A late answer can no longer replace the Sections you are writing yourself.
  • A message the AI could not answer comes back — if OpenRouter refuses a message or cannot be reached, your message goes back in the box with the reason, ready to send again, instead of going out again with every message after it.
  • Captions appear straight away on a paused video — turning captions on, correcting a line, adding subtitles, or captions finishing for a new take used to leave the old words on screen, or none at all, until you pressed play or moved the playhead. The new words now show the moment they change.
  • Fixing a caption no longer repeats words — if you retyped a line in the Captions list so it got longer, pressed Return and then clicked away, the words that spilled onto the next line could show up twice. Shortening a line could drop the first words of the next one. Now each fix is saved once.
  • Naming a Series makes one Recording — pressing Return twice quickly in the Name this Series box could make two Recordings when your Mac was busy. Now it makes one.
  • Saving right after you stop keeps the tidy-up — if you pressed Save Video as soon as you stopped recording, the video could be saved before iRecord had cut your pauses and ums, so it came out longer than the editor showed. Save Video now waits a moment for the tidy-up to finish, and says so.
  • A save that stops no longer leaves a big file behind — when Save Video stopped partway, or you cancelled it while it was stuck, it left a large unfinished file in the folder you were saving to, and you had to find and delete it yourself. Now iRecord deletes it.
  • Typing in a caption line no longer edits your video — while you corrected a line in the Captions list, ⌘Z undid your last timeline change instead of your typing, ⌘B cut the video, and the arrow keys moved the playhead instead of the cursor. Now those keys work on the text while you type, and go back to the timeline as soon as you click it.

item.title: Version 1.288.0
item.description:
What's New in 1.288.0

Added

  • Add a shadow under your video — the Padding panel has a new Shadow switch that puts a soft shadow under your video, in the editor and in the video you save. The editor used to show a shadow on every Recording that your saved video never had; now there is none until you add it.

Changed

  • Plan without the AI — the Create a Plan sheet has an AI switch at the top. Turn it off and there is no conversation: you type your Sections and see them listed with their lengths beside them. The sheet remembers your choice; until you make one, the AI is on only if you have connected an OpenRouter key.
  • Cursor zoom's level is a slider — instead of four fixed choices, you can now set how far the zoom goes anywhere from 1.5× to 3×. The Cursor Zoom panel also now puts the mode first and the three sliders under it.

Fixed

  • Saving no longer gets stuck partway — Save Video could stop moving partway through a Recording, most often one with many cuts, and never finish. Now it gets past the spot and saves the whole video.
  • A save that stops moving now stops and says so — Save Video could sit on the same percentage forever, and pressing Cancel then closed iRecord. Now a save that makes no progress for 30 seconds ends with a message, Cancel always brings you back, and your Recording is never touched either way.
  • Picture backgrounds show up in your saved videos — if a Recording had a picture as its background, the editor showed it, but the saved video and its poster frame had a plain black background instead. Now they show the picture, blurred and faded the way you set it.
  • Backgrounds look the same in the editor and in your saved video — gradients and see-through colours came out a little different in colour in the saved video, and a round gradient came out smaller. Now both look the same. In the editor, a round gradient may look smaller than before, and a blurred picture a little sharper: that is how your saved video will look.
  • Buttons near a picture background work again — with a tall picture as the background, some buttons stopped answering clicks: the Background panel's arrow and Choose Image button, Home and the Recording's name in the editor. On Home, a tall recording's thumbnail could block the bottom of the card above it. They all respond again.
  • Padding grows evenly as you drag — with Link sides on, dragging the padding slider added space above the picture first and only evened it out when you let go, which looked like a strange zoom. Now all four sides grow together while you drag.
  • The editor rounds corners and draws the camera border the way your saved video does — the editor rounded the corners of your screen and camera more than the saved video, drew a camera border thicker than in the file and half outside the camera, and on a tall or square video rounded the space around the picture instead of the picture itself. Now the editor matches the file.
  • No more thin lines at the edge of your camera or screen in the editor — at some padding values, and while you dragged the padding slider, a thin line could show along the top of the camera circle, or a dark line along the edges of your screen. They were never in your saved video, and now the editor doesn't show them either.

item.title: Version 1.285.0
item.description:
What's New in 1.285.0

Changed

  • New copies of iRecord come with a one-day trial — someone installing iRecord for the first time now gets one day to try it before buying, instead of seven. If you are already on a trial, nothing changes: you keep the seven days you started with.

item.title: Version 1.282.1
item.description:
What's New in 1.282.1

Added

  • Your takes come back already tidied — when you stop recording, the wait before your first word and after your last is trimmed, and pauses where nothing happened are shortened. On macOS 26, with captions on, your ums are cut too. The editor says how much shorter the video is and what was cut, and Undo All, there every time you open the Recording, puts it all back. You can turn this off in Settings → Recording.

Changed

  • A take's problem now shows where it is — instead of a small warning sign on the clip, the part of the clip that plays the problem is striped. Move the playhead into the stripes and a short line under the video says what is wrong there, with a Trim here button that ends the clip just before it.
  • Caption size is a slider — the Captions panel now sets how big your captions are with a slider instead of three buttons, and moves them between the bottom and the top with a switch. The panel reads in order: how captions look, what they say, then whether they go into the saved video. Recordings you already captioned keep the size they had.

Removed

  • Your iPhone shows up once in the camera list — an iPhone used as a camera without a cable used to appear twice, once as itself and once as Desk View, which films the desk from above and only works with the phone clipped to the top of your screen. Desk View is gone from the list, so picking your iPhone always gets the camera that films you.
  • Clicking a Section no longer covers the video with a script panel — the panel was for writing what to say, which is no help once a Section is recorded. Clicking a Section now just selects it, and you write a script on the Ready screen, before you record. The panel's Suggest talking points button went with it, and so did the Apple Intelligence line in Settings → AI.

Fixed

  • A saved video says when its captions have changed — if you changed the captions in a video after saving it (put them in or took them out, made them bigger or smaller, moved them, or corrected a line), the saved file still said it matched, so you couldn't tell it had the old captions. Now the list next to Save Video and the card on Home say Edited since saved. After this update, videos you already saved with captions in them will say so once, even though nothing is wrong with them; saving again clears it.
  • A paused iPhone or iPad recording no longer stops when the cable comes loose — if the cable slipped out while you were paused, iRecord didn't notice when you plugged it back in, kept trying to reconnect, and about half a minute later stopped the whole Recording while you were still paused. Now it sees the phone is back, says so, and waits for you, and when you resume, the take carries on where it left off. Time spent paused no longer counts toward the half a minute iRecord gives a cable to come back.
  • A Section you delete while recording no longer comes back — if you deleted a Section in the editor while iRecord was still recording into the same Recording, it came back when you moved on to the next Section or pressed Stop, without its video. Now the editor waits until you stop before it lets you change that Recording, and a new name you give it while recording is kept.
  • Opening a Recording while it records no longer loses Sections — if you opened a Recording from Home while iRecord was still recording into it, the Sections recorded after you opened it could vanish from the timeline once you stopped, and from the saved video too. Opening a different Recording while recording, then pressing Stop, could empty the timeline of the one you recorded. Now the editor shows every Section you recorded when you stop.
  • You can't delete a Recording while it is recording — deleting it threw away the video being recorded, and every Section after it. Now iRecord says it is being recorded and asks you to stop first.
  • Captions from a deleted take no longer turn up on the next one — if you deleted a Section while its captions were still being made, they could be saved anyway, then show up on the next take you recorded there and in its saved video. Now they are thrown away, and a new take never picks up captions that belong to a deleted one.
  • Undo works after deleting half of a split Section — if you split a clip and chose Delete Section on one half, iRecord warned that the take would be thrown away, which it wasn't, and then ⌘Z could no longer undo anything you had done. Now that half simply leaves the timeline, with no warning, and ⌘Z brings it back.
